---
title: "Contributing to nprcgenekeepr"
---

There are two ways to help. Anyone who uses the package can report a problem or
ask for a feature, which needs no setup and is covered in the first section. The
rest of this guide is for people comfortable with R packages who want to change
the code or the documentation.

Everyone taking part is asked to follow the
[code of conduct](https://github.com/rmsharp/nprcgenekeepr/blob/master/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

## Report a problem or ask for a feature

Colony managers see problems and needs that no test finds. All you need is a
free GitHub account: open an
[Issue](https://github.com/rmsharp/nprcgenekeepr/issues).

**For a problem,** please include:

- What you did: the steps in the app (which tab, which buttons) or the shortest
  script that shows the problem.
- What you expected, and what happened instead, with the exact wording of any
  error message.
- Your package version and R setup. Run these in R and paste the output:

```r
packageVersion("nprcgenekeepr")
sessionInfo()
```

Please show the problem with the package's example data, such as
`nprcgenekeepr::examplePedigree`, and do not post real colony records, because
Issues are public. If a problem appears only with your own file, make a small
made-up file with the same columns that shows it, or describe the columns and
values involved.

**For a feature,** please say what you are trying to do, what decision it would
help you make, and how you do it today.

## Set up a copy of the package

You need R, git and a C/C++ compiler (Xcode Command Line Tools on a Mac, Rtools
on Windows), because some packages may need building.

Fork the repository on GitHub, then clone your fork and open R in its folder:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/<your-account>/nprcgenekeepr.git
cd nprcgenekeepr
R
```

The project uses [renv](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/), which starts by itself
when R opens in this folder and keeps what you install here apart from your other
R libraries. Install what the package needs, then the development tools, and
answer yes when asked:

```r
renv::install(dependencies = "most", exclude = "Matrix")
renv::install(c("devtools", "lintr", "roxygen2@8.0.0"))
devtools::install(upgrade = FALSE)
```

`Matrix` is left out because it comes with R. These commands install current
versions of each package, as the automatic checks on a pull request do, with one
exception: `roxygen2` is the version the package's help pages were generated with,
because another version rewrites many of them. The last command installs your copy
of the package itself, which one of the tests needs.

To confirm it worked, load the package from your copy:

```r
pkgload::load_all()
```

After that, every function in `R/` is available, including ones not exported.
`runGeneKeepR()` starts the Shiny app from your copy.

## Where things live

| Path | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `R/` | The package's functions, mostly one to a file, with their help written as roxygen comments. |
| `R/appUI.R`, `R/appServer.R` | The Shiny app's layout and server. Each tab is a module in its own file, such as `R/modPedigree.R`. |
| `tests/testthat/` | The tests. `test_<name>.R` files are ordinary tests; `test-e2e-<name>.R` files drive the app in a browser. |
| `man/` | Help pages generated from the roxygen comments. Do not edit these by hand. |
| `vignettes/` | The tutorial and manual that install with the package, such as `vignettes/a2interactive.Rmd`. |
| `vignettes/articles/` | Articles for the website only, such as `vignettes/articles/colony-manager-guide.qmd`. |
| `inst/extdata/` | Example files, and in `inst/extdata/ui_guidance/` the help pages the app shows. |
| `data/`, `data-raw/` | Example datasets, and the scripts that build them. |
| `NEWS.Rmd` | The release notes. `NEWS.md` is generated from it. |
| `_pkgdown.yml` | The website's menus and its function reference. |

The other top-level files and folders hold the maintainer's working notes and
release records. A pull request does not need to touch them.

## Run the tests

To run one test file, which is what you will do most often:

```r
Sys.setenv(NOT_CRAN = "true")
pkgload::load_all()
testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test_kinship.R")
```

Setting `NOT_CRAN` matters: without it, a file that skips itself on CRAN does so
silently and looks as if it passed.

Before opening a pull request, run the whole suite and the package check:

```r
devtools::test()
devtools::check()
```

The browser tests are skipped unless you ask for them, because they need Chrome
and take much longer. They test the installed package rather than the loaded one,
so install your copy first. If you change something a tab shows, run the file for
that tab:

```r
devtools::install(upgrade = FALSE)
Sys.setenv(NOT_CRAN = "true", NPRC_RUN_E2E = "true")
testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-e2e-pedigree-module.R")
```

If the spelling test flags a word that is spelled correctly, add it to
`inst/WORDLIST`. Some other tests read the documentation itself, and a failure
there is telling you which page has fallen out of step.

## Write tests with your change

A pull request that changes what the package does includes tests for that change.
Cover the normal case, bad input, and the edge cases that matter for pedigrees,
such as an empty input, a single animal, or missing parents and dates. Aim to
cover more than 80% of the new code. Put the tests in
`tests/testthat/test_<name>.R`, using the file for the function you changed if
there is one:

```r
test_that("findOffspring gives 0 for an animal with no offspring", {
  ped <- data.frame(
    id = c("sire1", "dam1", "kid1"),
    sire = c(NA, NA, "sire1"),
    dam = c(NA, NA, "dam1")
  )
  counts <- findOffspring(c("sire1", "kid1"), ped)
  expect_identical(counts[["sire1"]], 1L)
  expect_identical(counts[["kid1"]], 0L)
})
```

To test a Shiny tab, use `shiny::testServer()` as the `test_mod<name>.R` files do.

We recommend writing the failing test first: run it, see it fail for the reason
you expect, write the smallest change that makes it pass, and then tidy up. This
is how most of the package was built, and it often finds a misunderstanding
before any code is written. It is not required of a pull request, as long as the
tests are there and they pass.

A new test file also runs during CRAN's check, which has a time limit. If yours
takes more than half a second, add its name to
`tests/testthat/slowTestFiles.txt`.

## Check style with lint

```r
pkgload::load_all()
lintr::lint_package()
```

This should report nothing. The rules are in `.lintr`, among them a limit of 80
characters per line; `tests/` and `vignettes/` are not linted.

## Update the documentation

Most changes need one or more of these:

- **A function's help.** Edit the roxygen comments in `R/`, then run
  `devtools::document()`, which regenerates `man/` and `NAMESPACE`. Check
  `git status` afterwards and commit only what belongs to your change.
- **A new exported function.** Add it to a reference group in `_pkgdown.yml`. A
  test fails until it is listed.
- **Anything a user would notice.** Add one plain line to `NEWS.Rmd`, under the
  section for the app tab it affects, then regenerate `NEWS.md`:

```r
rmarkdown::render("NEWS.Rmd", quiet = TRUE)
```

- **A change to what a tab shows or does.** Update that tab's part of
  `vignettes/articles/colony-manager-guide.qmd`, and its help page in
  `inst/extdata/ui_guidance/` if it has one.

## Propose a change

1. For anything larger than a small fix, open an
   [Issue](https://github.com/rmsharp/nprcgenekeepr/issues) first, so we can agree
   on the approach before you spend time on it.
2. Make your change on a new branch from `master`, keeping one change to a pull
   request.
3. Run the tests, the package check and lint, as above.
4. Open a pull request against `master`. Say what changed and why, and link the
   Issue if there is one.

Opening a pull request runs the package check, lint, test coverage and a website
build automatically, and the results appear on the pull request. The browser tests
run nightly on `master`, not on pull requests, so please run any that your change
affects yourself. The maintainer then reviews the pull request.
